properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-24: *"can we track all external dependencies in one file somewhere in reflow2? then every other file that needs an external dependency points to this as the master? ... Then when a new version of rust-rocksdb or rust-sdk (rmcp) or any other package comes out, we just have to update it in one location."*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ THE MECHANISM HE DESCRIBED ALREADY EXISTS — IT IS CARGO'S `[workspace.dependencies]`

The root `Cargo.toml` holds the version table; a crate writes `foo = { workspace = true }` instead of a version. Bump once, every crate follows. So the ANSWER to the question as asked is "yes, and it is built in."

🛑 **BUT THE MEASUREMENT SAYS IT IS BARELY USED, AND THAT IS THE REAL FINDING.** Counted 2026-08-24:

    [workspace.dependencies]                     8 crates
    reflow2-core   deps        8 workspace-ref   3 CRATE-LOCAL (serde, serde_json, sha2)
    reflow2-core   dev-deps    0 workspace-ref   2 CRATE-LOCAL (proptest, tempfile)
    reflow2-mcp    deps        0 workspace-ref  15 CRATE-LOCAL

⇒ **20 crate-local pins against 8 shared, and `reflow2-mcp` uses the table ZERO times.** Every dependency he named is crate-local: `rmcp` at `reflow2-mcp/Cargo.toml:24`, and `rocksdb` only reached the table today.

⚠️ **THE TABLE ONLY BECAME NON-TRIVIAL TODAY, AS A SIDE EFFECT.** Before the foundation absorption it held the two dynograph git pins and nothing else. The eight entries in it now are the crates the absorption brought in — they are there because that work needed somewhere to put them, not because anyone chose the pattern.

🛑 **FOUR CRATES ARE PINNED IN TWO PLACES INDEPENDENTLY** — `serde`, `serde_json`, `sha2` in both crates, and `tracing` now in the workspace table AND crate-local in `reflow2-mcp`. They agree today. Nothing makes them agree tomorrow, and nothing reports it if they stop: cargo resolves compatible ranges silently, so the first symptom of a drift is behavioural, not a build error.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, UNRANKED, each with what it costs

**A. MOVE EVERYTHING TO THE TABLE.** All 20 pins become `{ workspace = true }`.
   ⭐ Exactly what he asked for, and the four duplicate pins collapse to one each.
   ⚠️ It is also 20 lines of churn for a two-crate workspace where 15 of the 20 belong to ONE crate and no other crate will ever want them. A table of things only one consumer uses is a table of indirection.

**B. MOVE ONLY WHAT IS SHARED OR EXTERNALLY COUPLED.** The four duplicated pins, plus `rmcp` — the MCP SDK, the one dependency whose version is a protocol commitment rather than an implementation detail.
   ⭐ Smallest change that removes the real hazard: two places to bump one crate.
   ⚠️ Leaves a rule that has to be remembered — "shared ones go in the table" is a judgement nobody checks.

**C. LEAVE IT.** Crate-local pins are legitimate where one crate is the only consumer, and `reflow2-mcp` genuinely is for 15 of its 15.
   ⭐ The honest defence: a two-crate workspace is not where this bites. It bites at five.
   ⚠️ It does nothing about the four double pins, which are the part that is already wrong.

**D. DETECT IT RATHER THAN DECIDE IT.** A check that fails when one crate name is pinned in two places with two literals, or when a crate-local pin duplicates a table entry.
   ⭐ The only option that survives someone forgetting — and this project's own history says a rule with no detector decays. `tools/check_kit_manifest.py` and `check_doc_versions.py` are precedents for exactly this shape of gate.
   ⚠️ A gate for a two-crate workspace may be more machinery than the problem.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT

`rust-sdk` **IS** `rmcp` — the repository publishes that crate; they are not two things. `reflow2-mcp/Cargo.toml:61` already says so, which is why the commented-out `[patch]` block points at a local `rust-sdk` checkout.

📌 AND WHAT NOBODY HAS COSTED: whether any of the 20 pins currently resolve to different versions across the two crates. The four duplicates were compared as WRITTEN, not as RESOLVED — `Cargo.lock` would say, and nobody has read it for this.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2 has a workspace dependency table and one of its two crates never uses it: 20 crate-local pins against 8 shared, and four crates pinned twice
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-24, immediately after the rocksdb-version exchange. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

⭐ THE QUESTION HAD A FACTUAL ANSWER AND A REAL FINDING UNDERNEATH IT, and answering only the first would have been the mistake. "Can we track dependencies in one file?" is answered by "Cargo already does that" — and stopping there would have left 20 crate-local pins and four double-pinned crates unexamined. **A question that turns out to be already-solved is worth measuring anyway, because the answer is only true if the mechanism is used.**

🛑 IT WAS ALSO NEARLY LOST. The factual half was given in conversation and no node was written; it survives only because Anthony asked, two exchanges later, whether the ideas he had raised were being linked. That is the same failure `unreviewed_ideas` counts, one level up: not an idea recorded and unlinked, but an idea answered and never recorded at all.
